Judgment

1. The present appeal has been preferred impugning the order dated 24.05.2023 whereby the Ld.
ADM (South-East) reached to the conclusion that the appellant herein, who was respondent No.2 before the Ld. ADM, was guilty U/s. 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zx) of The Food Safety VIRENDER Digitally signed by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:19 +0530 and Standards Act, 2006 (in short FSS Act) and imposed a penalty of Rs.1,20,000/-.

2. The facts in brief giving rise to the present appeal are that on 25.05.2019 Ms. Anjali Bhardwaj, the Food Safety Officer, lifted the sample of "Buffalo Milk" from Ajay Kumar, the servant of the appellant herein.
The sample so lifted was put in four bottles and was sealed in accordance with the rules.
The sample was analyzed and was found deficient in milk solid not fat.
Accordingly, an application was filed before the Ld. ADM who passed an order dated 24.05.2023, which is impugned in the present appeal.

sentences.text: 3. Notice of the appeal was given to the State/FSO.
Record of the Ld. ADM was also summoned.
4. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the appellant, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State/FSO and perused the record.
5. Ld. Counsel submitted that the order passed by the Ld. ADM is not in accordance with rules and law and also not based upon the facts of the case resulting into miscarriage of justice.
Ld. Counsel submitted that in this case, according to the story of the prosecution, the samples were taken on 25.05.2019.

The report of the analyst has been received on 10.06.2019 and notice was given to Sh.
Ajay Kumar on 01.06.2019 giving him an opportunity to file appeal against the impugned order.

Ld.
Counsel submitted that as per Section 77 of the FSS Act, the limitation for Court to take cognizance is one year and no Court shall take cognizance after expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of the offence.

However, the Commissioner of Food Safety may for reasons to be recorded in writing VIRENDER VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:26 +0530 approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years.
Ld. Counsel submitted that delay has not been explained and the Court shall not condone the delay without any sufficient cause being shown.
Here in the present case, the prosecution has been initiated after one year and hence barred by limitation.

Ld. Counsel in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment cited as State of Uttar Pradesh through Executive Engineer and Another Vs. Amar Nath Yadav, [(2014) 2 SCC 422].
6.

Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that in this case the prosecution has been initiated within one year and there is no delay except due to the reason that Ms. Anjali Bhardwaj,
Food Safety Officer, who took the sample proceeded on maternity leave.

Para 10 of the application itself mentions the extension of time, which reads as under :
"That the Worthy Commissioner (Food Safety) granted extension time of 08 months beyond one year time limit under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards At,
2006 on request of the undersigned, which was forwarded by the Designated Officer concerned for completing pending investigation and launching prosecution."
7. Ld.

Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO has submitted that though the limitation is one year but the proviso to the Section empowers the Commissioner of Food Safety to extend the time and that has been done by the Commissioner of Food Safety and hence the prosecution, which has been launched on 16.07.2020 is within limitation.

It is submitted that there is no merit in the contentions raised and on that ground no benefit can be given to the appellant herein.

sentences.text: After hearing the arguments and going through the record, I found that U/s.77 of the FSS Act, it is specifically provided that no Court shall take cognizance under this Act after the expiry of period of one year from the date of commission of the offence.
The Section also provides that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for the reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years.
This clearly shows that the Commissioner of Food Safety may in appropriate cases extend the period of prosecution beyond the period of one year and such period may extend upto three years.
However, Commissioner Food Safety has to give reasons in writing to extend this period.

Keeping in view the present position, it is clear that cognizance cannot be taken beyond one year but the law also provides/authorizes the Commissioner of Food Safety to extend the time and it has been mentioned in the petition itself that the Commissioner had extended the time considering all the facts.

Hence, on this count, in my opinion, no benefit can be given to the appellant herein as the Commissioner has extended the period for 08 months as mentioned in para 10 of the application filed before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer.
Keeping in view this position, in my opinion, on this count no benefit can be extended to the appellant.

9. Ld. Counsel further submitted that the appellant has not received the copy of the report of food analyst along with notice U/s.46(4) of the Act, which is mandatory in nature and he has been deprived of his valuable right.

Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that the Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011,
Rule 2.4.1.4 provides as under :
VIRENDER by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:46 +0530 "2.4: Sampling and Analysis 2.4.1: Procedure for taking sample and manner of sending it for analysis - The Food Safety Officer while taking sample of food for analysis under clause A of Sub Section 1 of Section 38 and Section 47 (except 47 (5)) of the Act, shall also follow the procedure specified hereunder;-
4. in case the food business operator discloses that the product has been obtained from the manufacturer, the distributor or supplier, a notice shall also be given to such manufacturer, distributor or supplier."
11.

sentences.text: Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that in this case person who was found on the spot at the time of taking the sample had not disclosed the name of the appellant herein and hence the notice cannot be given to him.

Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO further submitted that Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011 and 2.4.5. further provides as under :
"2.4.5: Food business operator's right to have the food analysed 1.

In case the Food business operator from whom the sample has been taken or the person whose name and address and other particulars have been disclosed under Rule 2.5 of these rules, desires to have the fourth part of the sample analysed, he shall request the Food Safety Officer in writing to send the sample to any NABL accredited/ FSSAI notified laboratory for analysis under intimation to the Designated Sunil Baisoya vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158401646/
3 Officer.

sentences.text: The Food Safety Officer shall send the sample to a NABL accredited/FSSAI notified laboratory, under intimation to the Designated Officer forthwith, in the manner prescribed under Rule 2.4.1.
Provided that the cost of testing by the accredited lab will be borne by the Food Business Operator or the person identified under Rule 2.5.
The payment shall be made by the Food Business Operator through Bank draft or online transfer or treasury chalan or any other suitable means as specified by the Designated Officer.

Provided further that the Accredited lab where the Food Safety Officer will send the sample, should be within the Digitally signed VIRENDER by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:54 +0530 state or the neighboring state wherever available 3.

The Food Analyst in-charge of the accredited laboratory shall analyse the sample within fourteen days from the date of the receipt of the sample;
Provided that in case the sample cannot be analysed within fourteen days from the date of its receipt, the Food Analyst/in-charge of the accredited laboratory, shall inform the Designated Officer and the Commissioner of Food Safety giving reasons and specify the time to be taken for analysis.
4. The Food Analyst shall send four copies of the analysis report to the Designated Officer, in the proforma given in Form VII A, indicating the method of analysis".
12.

Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that as in this case Ajay Kumar, who was found on the shop at the time of taking the sample, has not disclosed at all that it was the appellant herein who was the owner hence the notice could not be sent to him and the moment it was brought to their notice he was immediately contacted and informed.
The fact that he was contacted and informed is evident from the record itself.
This contention that he was not given any notice is not correct.

The fact that he received the notice is evident from the fact that he has send the reply dated 30.07.2020 wherein he stated that he is the proprietor of Sangam Dairy and Ajay Kumar, Food Business Operator was his employee who was looking after the dairy.

Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that this fact clearly shows that he was given notice immediately thereafter and even the Court has sent him the summons, which are available on record dated VIRENDER Digitally signed by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date:
2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:38:01 +0530 09.11.2022, 15.02.2023, 03.04.2023 and 08.05.2023.
Pursuance to these summons, Ajay Kumar put appearance who was employee of the appellant but the appellant chose not to appear.

Summons to the appellant herein were sent at the address of his dairy also and the address, which he has provided in his reply and at his residential address, which he has provided in the form of Aadhar Card annexed with the reply dated 30.07.2020 i.e. P-133,

Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that keeping in view all these facts, this contention that he was not supplied the copy as mandatory or that summons were not sent to him is not substantiated by the evidence available on record and hence on this ground no benefit be given to him.
14.
After going through the record and the rules, I found that Ajay Kumar had not told that owner of the shop is Sunil Baisoya appellant herein.
In the absence of the same, it was not in the knowledge of the FSO or the authorities that it is the appellant herein to whom copy has to be sent.

It is specifically provided under the Rules that in case the Food Business Operator discloses the name of the manufacturer, distributor or supplier, the notice be also given to such manufacturer, distributor or supplier about the present owner.

Similarly, his right to get it analyzed is also coupled with the same as the Rule 2.4.5 further provides that, "in case the Food Business Operator or the person whose name and address has been disclosed under Rule 2.5 desires to have the forth part of the sample analyzed, he can do so".
But here no such declaration has been made.
The record also shows that notice was served on him and he also sent the reply but at that time, he has not requested that the sample be sent for analysis.
The summons were sent even by the VIRENDER Digitally VIRENDER signed by KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL

Adjudicating Authority but he chose not to appear and, therefore, now he cannot be allowed to complain that he was not given an opportunity as he himself continued to sleep and did not choose to apply for re-analyzing or taking any defence before the Adjudicating Authority.
15. Ld. Counsel submitted that there is only marginal variation as per the report of the analyst.

The standard provided is that milk solid not fat shall not be less than 9.0% and as per the test conducted,
the same was found to be 7.27%.
There is only marginal variation of 1.73% hence the Adjudicating Authority should have considered that fact that it is only a marginal variation and given benefit to him.
Ld. Counsel submitted that such marginal variation can be due to wrong sampling or even due to analytical error and hence benefit be given to him.

Ld. Counsel in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment cited as Delhi Administration Vs. Balak Ram [(2024) (2) FAC 49] wherein the difference in milk solid not fat were analyzed and there was variation of .2% and given the benefit.

entities.text: Delhi Administration Vs. Balak Ram [(2024) (2) FAC 49]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that firstly it is not marginal variation.
In the case relied upon by the appellant, the variation was only .2% whereas here the variation is 1.73%.
It cannot fall in the category of marginal difference or variation.
The method has been followed as prescribed.
The analyst has followed the recognized method of analysis i.e. AOAC official method 990.21 for analyzing presence of milk solids not fat in the samples.
It is a well recognized method.
No fault can be found with the same.

It is prayed that under the circumstances and keeping in view the fact that is not marginal variation but it is a large violation, hence no benefit be VIRENDER by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:38:16 +0530 extended to him.
Counsel has also submitted that AOAC official method 990.21 is not the recognized method but he could not produce any such material on record that it is not a recognized method for analysis.
The presence of milk solids not fat in the milk sample.

According to the report, the required percentage of the milk solid not fat in the milk was not to be less than 9%, whereas in the sample, it Sunil Baisoya vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158401646/
5 was found to be 7.27%.

sentences.text: The variation is 1.73% and cannot be said to be a marginal variation and hence in my opinion, on this count no benefit can be given to the appellant herein.
18. Ld. Counsel further submitted that in this case the facsimile of the seal used and the sealed samples was not immediately sent to the data analyst for analysis and have not tallied the same.
19. I have gone through the report of the analyst and also the record.

20. The analyst report, which is available on the record shows that the sample sealed as well as sample seal were sent and the report read as under :
"seals were intact and identical to the specimen impression of the seal received from the Food Officer".
21.
Hence, this contention that sample seal was not sent is not correct.

It is also pertinent to mention here that there is no cross-examination of the food analyst or of the Food Safety Officer, in this case,
under the circumstances merely raising an objection without any substance or the fact will not serve any purpose.
On this count also, in my opinion, no benefit can VIRENDER Digitally signed by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:38:25 +0530 be given to the appellant.
22. In the present case, the sample of the Buffalo Milk was lifted by the Food Safety Officer from Sangam Dairy being run by the appellant herein.
Notice was also sent to the appellant herein to which he replied on 30.07.2020.
The Adjudicating Authority also send the notices to him, but he choose not to appear.

The Adjudicating Authority after considering all the facts and the report,
which shows that the milk solids not fat in the sample was less than the standard prescribed i.e.
7.27% against 9%, held him guilty and imposed the penalty.
23. In view of all these facts, the Adjudicating officer rightly decided against the appellant and imposed the penalty.
There is no merit in the appeal.
The same is dismissed.
Record of the Ld. ADM be returned along with copy of this judgment.
Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
